column3: NASB renders “Christ” as “Messiah” here, and turns “book of the genealogy” into “record of the genealogy.”
NASB renders “begat” throughout as “was the father of.”
NASB supplies the name “Bathsheba”; the Greek says only “her of Uriah.” “The king” after the second “David” is a Textus Receptus word and is not translated.
NASB has “Asa,” the Textus Receptus spelling; the critical text reads “Asaph.”
NASB has “Asa” for the critical text’s “Asaph” (see v. 7).
NASB has “Amon,” the Textus Receptus spelling; the critical text reads “Amos.”
“Was found having in the womb from the Holy Spirit” becomes “found to be with child by the Holy Spirit”; “origin” is rendered “birth.”
NASB supplies “the Child”; the Greek has “that which has been conceived in her.”
NASB prints the Old Testament quotation in capitals; “have in the womb” becomes “be with child.”
“Was not knowing her” is rendered “kept her a virgin.” NASB follows the critical text with “a Son”; “her firstborn” is from the Textus Receptus.
